--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.edge_dfs()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Traverse every edge reachable from a source in depth-first order. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.edge_dfs()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Traverse every edge reachable from a source in depth-first order. title: >- [Graph.edge_dfs()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Traverse every edge reachable from a source in depth-first order. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Traverse every edge reachable from a source in depth-first order. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L64865-L64955){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.edge_dfs( source=None, orientation=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Edge DFS](../assets/graphs/edge-dfs.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The directed triangle A to B to C to A plus a fourth edge A to C, searched depth-first from A (outlined). The numbered accent arrows give the visit order: the search dives A to B, B to C and C back to A, then takes the remaining edge A to C fourth. The card lists the four edges beside dfs_edges, which keeps only (A, B) and (B, C)." width="100%"} The depth-first counterpart of `edge_bfs()`: every edge reachable from the source is visited exactly once, following each new edge as deep as possible before backtracking. This is the traversal NetworkX's `find_cycle` builds on, and it suits Euler-style walks and edge-by-edge exploration of directed graphs. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str, list, None]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A start node, a list of start nodes, or `None` (default) for all nodes, in ID order. [orientation]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : `None` (default), `"original"`, `"reverse"` or `"ignore"`, as in `edge_bfs()`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[tuple]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The edges in visit order as `(u, v, edge_id)` triples, with a fourth `"forward"`/`"reverse"` element when `orientation` is given. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If a node does not exist or `orientation` is invalid. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Iterative depth-first search over edges with a per-node edge iterator. $O(V + E)$. Matches NetworkX's `edge_dfs`. ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~dfs_edges`) : Only the edges that reach a new node. [](`~edge_bfs`) : Every edge in breadth-first order. [](`~dfs_labeled_edges`) : Every step of the search, labeled by kind. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Every edge reachable from A is visited once, the edge back from C to A included: ::: {#61686c63 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph.from_edges( [("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("A", "C")], directed=True ) label = graph.get_label_from_id [(label(u), label(v)) for u, v, _ in graph.edge_dfs("A")] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [('A', 'B'), ('B', 'C'), ('C', 'A'), ('A', 'C')] ``` ::: ::: ### Everything a paper builds on `citations()` links each paper of a made-up research field to the earlier papers it cites. Following citations from Kim 2017 reaches every citation among the papers it builds on, directly or not: ::: {#26629ea4 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} papers = ec.citations() links = papers.edge_dfs("Kim 2017") len(links) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 39 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#fa5fbebc .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} papers.plot( layout="pos", highlight_edges=[e for _, _, e in links], label_by="label", ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: With `orientation="reverse"`, the search follows the citations backward, from Moreau 2000 to every paper that builds on it: ::: {#e5b37ee9 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} later = papers.edge_dfs("Moreau 2000", orientation="reverse") len(later) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` 44 ``` ::: :::
